    {
      "codeBlock": {
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "lineNumber": 27148,
            "text": "- **SectionChips**: Collapsible cards for location and category selections - **SectionMore** (unit, project) will be styled as a smaller card."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27149
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27150,
            "text": "The section order prioritizes user focus:"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27151,
            "text": "1. Sticky strip showing current selection"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27152,
            "text": "2. **Name** section (hero) - prioritized for immediate attention"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27153,
            "text": "3. Quick picks (last used + frequently selected)"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27154,
            "text": "4. Barcode, photo, and quantity in a single \"meta\" band"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27155,
            "text": "5. Collapsible \"all locations\" section with filter"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27156,
            "text": "6. Collapsible \"all categories\" section with filter"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27157,
            "text": "7. Unit and project sections with filters, potentially collapsible if extensive User didn't ask - I'll add search for unit and project in same expanded areas."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27158
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27159,
            "text": "Reorder: **Name first**, then same as last / often used (shortcuts), then barcode/photo/qty, then collapsible all lists."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27160
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27161,
            "text": "Current order has same as last before name - I'll swap to put Name block first after strip."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27162
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27163,
            "text": "Implementing."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27164
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27165,
            "text": "State additions:"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27166,
            "text": "- allLocOpen, setAllLocOpen - initialize in hydrate"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27167,
            "text": "- allCatOpen, setAllCatOpen  "
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27168,
            "text": "- locFilter, catFilter, unitFilter, projFilter - strings"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27169
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27170,
            "text": "Filtered lists:"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27171,
            "text": "- filteredLocationsTop"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27172,
            "text": "- filteredCategoriesTop"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27173,
            "text": "- filteredUnitsTop"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27174,
            "text": "- filteredProjectsTop Filtered lists now include location and category paths with case-insensitive search. Sub-locations are filtered when parent locations are selected. Favorite chips do not require filtering at this time. Search inputs are added for unit and project sections. The hydrate logic sets initial open states for locations and categories based on saved values."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27175
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27176,
            "text": "- Location and category filters update lists dynamically"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27177,
            "text": "- Favorite chips remain unfiltered for simplicity"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27178,
            "text": "- Unit and project sections get small search inputs"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27179,
            "text": "- Hydration logic sets initial open states based on saved data If &#96;cat&#96; can be an empty string, then &#96;!cat&#96; evaluates to true, which would expand the category section when no category is selected. The &#96;saveLast&#96; function stores the current location, category, unit, project, and name in persistent storage."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27180
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27181,
            "text": "The strip layout will be a compact single line containing three buttons with text only for clarity, using appropriate icons if desired. The selection strip uses a grid layout with three equal columns on wide screens or stacks on narrow screens. It contains three buttons with text only, using appropriate icons like ChevronDown, ChevronRight, MapPin, Tag, and Box or Layers from lucide. The collapsible component will follow shadcn standards, and stub imports will be skipped if not needed. The implementation plan involves restructuring the component in chunks rather than a single large edit to reduce errors. During hydration, the component sets initial states for location and category open states using &#96;setAllLocOpen&#96; and &#96;setAllCatOpen&#96; based on the saved location (&#96;loc&#96;) and category (&#96;cat&#96;) values. The logic uses direct variable checks: &#96;setAllLocOpen(!locFinal)&#96; and &#96;setAllCatOpen(!cat)&#96;, where &#96;locFinal&#96; is the final location value after any potential modifications. State updates occur asynchronously, so the original &#96;loc&#96; and &#96;cat&#96; variables are used directly for determining open states. Additional state setters include &#96;setCategory&#96;, &#96;applyLocationId&#96;, &#96;setUnit&#96;, &#96;setProject&#96;, and &#96;setName&#96;. The component also initializes filters and handles last-used data loading via &#96;applyLastName&#96; and &#96;saveLast&#96; functions. If &#96;loc&#96; is an empty string, &#96;!loc&#96; evaluates to true, which expands the location sectionthis is the intended behavior."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27182
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27183,
            "text": "When the dialog opens, filters are reset:"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27184,
            "text": "- &#96;setLocFilter(\"\")&#96;"
          }
        ],

          }

          {
            "lineNumber": 27609,
            "text": "- **Unit \u0026 project** — One panel with a dashed split between unit and project."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27610
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27611,
            "text": "**Sticky selection strip** (under the title, above the scroll)  "
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27612,
            "text": "- **Current**: three tappable cells — location, category, unit (truncated, with icons). Tapping opens the matching **All locations** / **All categories** section (and expands it) or scrolls to **Unit \u0026 project**.  "
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27613,
            "text": "- **Go to**: **Name**, **Shortcuts**, **Details** — smooth-scroll to those sections."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27614
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27615,
            "text": "**Collapsible lists**  "
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27616,
            "text": "- **All locations** and **All categories** use a header row + chevron; body expands/collapses.  "
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27617,
            "text": "- On each dialog open, &#96;hydrate()&#96; sets &#96;allLocOpen&#96; / &#96;allCatOpen&#96; to **open when that value is missing**, otherwise **closed**.  "
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27618,
            "text": "- When collapsed, a one-line summary shows the current selection or “Collapsed — tap header to expand.”"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27619
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27620,
            "text": "**Search**  "
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27621,
            "text": "- Filter fields above: all locations (including sub-areas when the parent is expanded), all categories, units, projects.  "
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27622,
            "text": "- Empty filter results show a short “No … match” line."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27623
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27624,
            "text": "**Last name**  "
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27625,
            "text": "- &#96;LastSnapshot&#96; now includes optional &#96;name&#96;; it is written on successful submit.  "
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27626,
            "text": "- **Last name** appears in the Name row when a stored name exists; it fills the field and focuses the input."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27627
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27628,
            "text": "&#96;npx tsc --noEmit&#96; passes."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27629
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27630,
            "text": "---"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27631
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27632,
            "text": "_**User**_"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27633
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27634,
            "text": "I like it. the collapable sections can also be used for Unit and Project."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27635
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27636,
            "text": "I like the way the subcategories are handles, let's use that for the sections such as Unit and others as well."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27637
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27638
          },

            "lineNumber": 27639
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27640,
            "text": "---"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27641
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27642,
            "text": "_**Agent (default)**_"

          {
            "lineNumber": 27643
          },
          {

            "text": "\u003cthink\u003e\u003cdetails\u003e\u003csummary\u003eThought Process\u003c/summary\u003e"

          {

            "text": "The user wants to make Unit and Project collapsible, similar to All locations and All categories, with expand/collapse functionality, filtering when expanded, and summary display when collapsed."
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27646
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27647,
            "text": "- Implement collapsible sections for Unit and Project"

            "text": "- Enable filtering within expanded sections"

            "text": "The strip layout will be a compact single line containing three buttons with text only for clarity, using appropriate icons if desired. The selection strip uses a grid layout with three equal columns on wide screens or stacks on narrow screens. It contains three buttons with text only, using appropriate icons like ChevronDown, ChevronRight, MapPin, Tag, and Box or Layers from lucide. The collapsible component will follow shadcn standards, and stub imports will be skipped if not needed. The implementation plan involves restructuring the component in chunks rather than a single large edit to reduce errors. During hydration, the component sets initial states for location and category open states using &#96;setAllLocOpen&#96; and &#96;setAllCatOpen&#96; based on the saved location (&#96;loc&#96;) and category (&#96;cat&#96;) values. The logic uses direct variable checks: &#96;setAllLocOpen(!locFinal)&#96; and &#96;setAllCatOpen(!cat)&#96;, where &#96;locFinal&#96; is the final location value after any potential modifications. State updates occur asynchronously, so the original &#96;loc&#96; and &#96;cat&#96; variables are used directly for determining open states. Additional state setters include &#96;setCategory&#96;, &#96;applyLocationId&#96;, &#96;setUnit&#96;, &#96;setProject&#96;, and &#96;setName&#96;. The component also initializes filters and handles last-used data loading via &#96;applyLastName&#96; and &#96;saveLast&#96; functions. If &#96;loc&#96; is an empty string, &#96;!loc&#96; evaluates to true, which expands the location sectionthis is the intended behavior."

            "text": "          \u003cp\u003eAudit logs prioritize state-changing operations (item create/edit/delete, check-in/out, user/config changes).\u003c/p\u003e"
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 214,
            "text": "          \u003cp\u003ePerformance logs cover heavy operations (report export and bulk actions).\u003c/p\u003e"

          },

### Lookup lists (collapsible groups)

Parent rows in `EditableItemWithSubcategoriesList` now start **collapsed** when they have sub-locations. Adding a new sub-location **expands** that row so the new entry is visible.

### Settings snapshot (JSON) — how to restore

Under **Settings → Data Management → Backup & Restore → “Settings snapshot (JSON)”** there is now **Restore settings snapshot** next to download. Choose a file exported earlier (`trackIT-settings-snapshot_….json` with `"version": "trackIT-settings-snapshot"`).

That restore **replaces** lookup lists, financial codes, cabinets, and general preferences from the file. It **does not** change inventory rows (those stay as they are); use **Import & Export** or a full **.backup** workflow for inventory.

### Daily offline backups

In the same **Backup & Restore** card, under **Create Backup**, **Daily offline backup** toggles automatic behavior: while the app is open, once per **local calendar day** it downloads a **full** JSON backup (lists, inventory, financial codes, preferences, cabinets, templates) as `trackIT-daily-backup_YYYY-MM-DD.backup` and records the date. Downloads go through the browser’s normal download folder.

### Decommissioning

- **Item form → Additional Info**: **EOL target date**, **Cut-over scheduled**, **Last lifecycle audit**, and **Audit / EOL / cut-over notes**.
- **Asset status**: new **Cut-over pending** value.
- **Reports → Decommissioning & cut-over**: built-in report with rack + lifecycle columns.
- **Inventory (detailed columns)**: **Rack** column.

### Rack location

On **Item Details**, when the location is a sub-location whose label ends with **`/TE`**, **`/Imagine`**, or **`/ITV`** (matching your tree names), **Rack location** offers presets:

- **TE**: rows **TX, TC, TD, TE, TF, TG, TH, TJ, TK** with rack numbers from your diagram (e.g. `TX-06` … `TX-17`, `TC-13` … `TC-01`, merged **TD** top + main as **TD-15** … **TD-01**, etc.).
- **Imagine**: **CA-2** … **CA-6**, **CB-2** … **CB-6**.
- **ITV**: **IA**–**ID** with racks **1**–**6** each.

**Custom…** allows any free-text rack id if something is not in the list. Changing **Location** clears rack and cabinet as before.

Relevant areas: ```98:99:src/components/EditableItemWithSubcategoriesList.tsx``` (default collapsed), ```263:325:src/components/settings/DataBackupTab.tsx``` (daily backup + snapshot restore), ```546:598:src/pages/SettingsPage.tsx``` (`handleRestoreSettingsSnapshot`), ```1:74:src/lib/rackLocations.ts```, ```9:26:src/types/inventory.ts``` (new fields + `cut_over_pending`), ```44:56:src/App.tsx``` (daily backup scheduler).

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
When constructing URLs for fetch requests, if the base URL is `/`, the resulting URL becomes `/config/rack-locations`. When constructing URLs, using `.replace(/\/{2,}/g, "/")` can incorrectly modify `https://` protocols; a safer approach is to use `.replace(":/", "://")` as a hack, though it's fragile.

A better solution uses:
- `const base = (import.meta.env.BASE_URL || "/").replace(/\/$/, "");`
- `const path = `${base}/config/rack-locations.json`.replace(/\/+/g, "/");`

This avoids issues with empty base values and ensures proper URL construction.

Alternative method:
- `new URL('config/rack-locations.json', window.location.origin + base).href`</details></think>

Here is what was implemented:

### Units & tagging placement
In `BasicDetailsTab`, **Units & tagging** is now in the **left column**, directly under **Asset status** (same tab as before).

### Edit dialog position (no vertical jump)
`EditItemDialog` now uses the same pattern as **Add New Inventory Item**: top-anchored `DialogContent` (`!top-[max(0.5rem,6vh)]`, `!translate-y-0`, slide from top), **header in a fixed strip**, and **scrollable body** so changing tabs / height does not re-center the modal.

### Rack locations from config (not hardcoded)
- **Bundled default:** `src/config/rack-locations.default.json` — shipped with the app; edit in-repo for your facility.
- **Runtime override:** `public/config/rack-locations.json` — same JSON shape; replace on disk after build to change racks without rebuilding. Loaded on startup via `refreshRackLocationsFromServer()` in `App.tsx` (`src/lib/rackLocationsConfig.ts`).

Schema: `{ "version": 1, "rules": [ { "subLocation": "te", "options": ["TX-06", ...] }, ... ] }`. The last segment of the location label (e.g. `TE` in `Server Rooms / TE`) is matched to `subLocation` case-insensitively.

### Searchable location & rack (type “TD…”)
- **Location** and **rack** on the item form use the existing **`Combobox`** (search-as-you-type). Rack allows **custom values** when the list does not include what you need.
- Popover list sizing is tightened in `combobox.tsx` (`max-h`, min width tied to trigger where Radix exposes it).

### Quick Add
- **Dialog** uses the same **top-anchored** positioning so it does not jump.
- **All locations:** a **Search location** combobox at the top (full flat list, type-to-filter) plus the existing chip filter.
- **Details:** **Asset status**, **Units & tagging**, then **Rack** (searchable combobox when the config applies), then barcode / photo / quantity. Payload includes `assetStatus`, `assetTrackingMode`, and `rackLocation`. Changing location clears rack; **Add next** clears rack after a successful add.

Files to know: `src/components/BasicDetailsTab.tsx`, `src/components/EditItemDialog.tsx`, `src/components/MobileQuickAddDialog.tsx`, `src/lib/rackLocationsConfig.ts`, `src/config/rack-locations.default.json`, `public/config/rack-locations.json`, `src/components/ui/combobox.tsx`, `src/App.tsx`.

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The issue involves standard cmdk behavior where `onSelect` receives values with normalized characters, typically lowercased, when calling onSelect. So when using CommandItem with onSelect, the issue might not be with how option.value is passed, but rather how onSelect interacts with other components like CommandEmpty. The problem could stem from:

- CommandEmpty being a sibling component that may interfere with click events
- The onSelect handler not firing properly due to component interaction issues

The user is passing option.value directly to handleSelect, which should work correctly. **cmdk issue with `value` containing special characters** - location IDs like `1734567890/1734567891` might cause problems due to spaces or slashes.

**The real bug**: In cmdk v1+, `CommandItem`'s `value` is used for internal filtering. When `onSelect` is called, cmdk passes **transformed** value to onSelect in some versions. However, the arrow function `() => handleSelect(option.value)` should correctly capture the `option.value` through closure.

**Dialog form**: Edit dialog is inside a form - click propagation as submit is unlikely for CommandItem. **Pointer events on Popover inside scrollable Dialog** - could be related to overflow or z-index issues.

**CommandEmpty always visible**: In cmdk, CommandEmpty shows when there are no matching items from cmdk's internal filter. Setting `shouldFilter={false}` affects how items are filtered, but CommandEmpty may still render based on the command's filtered list. Need to verify if CommandEmpty behavior changes with `shouldFilter={false}`.

Reading cmdk source behavior: When `shouldFilter={false}`, the Command primitive might still process value internally, even if it doesn't filter items. CommandEmpty renders only when there are no search results.

With `shouldFilter={false}`, all items are considered visible, but CommandEmpty might still render in the DOM and potentially overlay content.

According to cmdk docs, CommandEmpty should not render when filteredOptions has items.

Potential bug: Custom filter logic may incorrectly trigger CommandEmpty rendering despite having results. - CommandItem `value` must be unique and avoid spaces, as cmdk lowercases values for matching, which can cause issues if `onSelect` relies on the original value.
- The `onSelect` callback receives the lowercased value, but since the code uses an arrow function `() => handleSelect(option.value)`, it correctly captures the original value via closure.
- If `onSelect` isn't firing at all, the issue may lie in event handling or focus management.
- Radix Dialog's focus trap may interfere with interactions within nested components like Popover. Popover inside Dialog can have pointer events issues due to Radix's focus trap or pointer-events blocking interaction.  
- Use `modal={false}` on Popover or implement portaling with `container` prop.  
- Alternatively, adjust Dialog's modal behavior to allow proper interaction.  
- The issue may also stem from focus trapping preventing Popover content from receiving events.</details></think>

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The Dialog component from Radix UI causes Popover portals to the body with z-50 when "Edit inventory" is inside a Dialog. Popover rendering behind dialog overlay is likely due to stacking context issues, since both use z-50 or higher. The popover portals to the body, making clicks inside it register as outside the dialog content from the DOM perspective, which prevents selection despite search working properly.

- Radix Dialog's `onPointerDownOutside` prevents dismissal on outside clicks
- Popover portals to document, so clicks inside popover are considered outside dialog content
- Search functionality works but item clicks don't select items When a user clicks a CommandItem in the popover, Radix Dialog interprets it as an outside pointer down, potentially focusing the dialog, closing the popover, or preventing the click from reaching the item. This is a well-known issue where Combobox/Popover inside Dialog causes events to be intercepted by the Dialog's dismissable layer or focus trap, since the popover is portaled outside the DialogContent in the DOM tree.

Fix options include:
- Setting `modal={false}` on the Dialog (though this impacts UX)

Here is what was going wrong and what we changed.

**Cause:** The location field uses a **Popover + cmdk** combobox. That UI is rendered in a **portal** (next to `document.body`), not inside the dialog’s DOM node. Radix **Dialog** still treats pointer events on that portaled layer as **“outside”** the dialog. It intercepts them (focus / dismiss logic), so **`CommandItem` never receives a proper click** even though the list looks fine.

**Fix (global on all dialogs):** In `dialog.tsx`, `DialogContent` now runs **`onInteractOutside`** and **`onPointerDownOutside`** handlers that call **`preventDefault()`** when the event target is inside Radix portaled layers (`[data-radix-popper-content-wrapper]`, select content, dropdown menu content). Clicks on the combobox list are no longer treated as outside the dialog, so items can be selected.

**Extra hardening:** In `combobox.tsx`, the list is wrapped in **`CommandList`** (what cmdk expects), and each **`CommandItem`** uses a **composite `value`** (`label + unicode space + id`) so internal cmdk value handling stays stable while **`onSelect` still applies the real `option.value`**.

After a refresh, choosing **Server Rooms/TE** (or any row) from the search list should set **Location** and close the popover as expected.

Spreading `{...props}` after `onFocusOutside` may override the handler if `props` includes `onFocusOutside`. In React, later props override earlier ones, so spreading `{...props}` after handlers could overwrite the intended behavior if `props` includes those handlers. Currently, the order is:

- `{...props}`

This means that if a user passes `onFocusOutside` in `props`, it would be overridden by our explicit handler chain. **Critical finding**: `DialogContentModal` has `disableOutsidePointerEvents: true` set on the Dialog's DismissableLayer! Because `DialogContentModal` disables pointer events outside itself, the popover (which is portaled outside the dialog) cannot receive clicks. This blocks interactions with command items in the popover.

**Solution options**:
- Move the popover inside the dialog's content area
- Adjust pointer-events to allow interaction with the popover
- Reconsider the portal placement of the popover Setting `modal={false}` on Dialog Root for AddItemDialog and MobileQuickAddDialog removes scroll lock and focus trap benefits, or requires using non-modal dialogs.

Portaling the popover inside DialogContent ensures it stays within the dialog's dismissable layer area, allowing pointer events to work properly. This requires verifying that the dismissable layer accounts for descendants within the content area.

Radix may provide a **Nested** pattern to handle such scenarios. The cleanest fix for shadcn is to use **`Dialog` with `modal={false}`** for dialogs containing popovers, such as AddItemDialog and MobileQuickAddDialog.

This prevents the `disableOutsidePointerEvents: true` issue that blocks popover interactions.

Downside: The overlay won't block clicks to the page behind, though a visual overlay remains.

**Fix**: Set `modal={false}` on AddItemDialog and MobileQuickAddDialog (and potentially EditItemDialog). When `modal={false}`, the `DialogOverlay` doesn't render because it's conditionally rendered only when `context.modal` is true. This means the dimmed background overlay is lost, which might be acceptable depending on requirements.

A better solution is to portal the combobox content **into** the dialog content element. By setting the `Radix Popover.Portal`'s `container` prop to the scrollable div inside the dialog, the popover renders within the dialog's DOM structure  avoiding pointer event issues since it's no longer "outside" the dialog's dismissable layer.</details></think>

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
manufacturerNotes is not part of InventoryItem but is added at runtime through addItem and exists as an extra property on runtime objects, though TypeScript is unaware of this. For the edit form, add optional fields manufacturerNotes and additionalNotes to InventoryItem, or map additionalNotes to notes when saving. The simplest approach is to:

- Add manufacturerNotes and additionalNotes to EditItemForm schema
- Use shared AdditionalInfoTab with additionalNotes field, wiring defaultValues from item.notes and mapping to notes on save
- Add optional manufacturerNotes and additionalNotes to InventoryItem for consistency with stored data

Alternatively, keep single notes field and map additionalNotes to notes on save. - Form field `additionalNotes` is used in edit forms, defaulting to `item.notes`
- On save, `additionalNotes` is mapped to `notes` for storage
- `manufacturerNotes` can be sourced from `item.manufacturerNotes` or added to the `InventoryItem` type
- Alternatively, keep `notes` as the persisted field and only use `additionalNotes` in forms, mapping it to `notes` on save
- Template forms map `data.additionalNotes` to `notes` for template storage - Save `notes: values.additionalNotes`
- Form field `manufacturerNotes` defaults to `item.manufacturerNotes` or empty string
- Save `manufacturerNotes` to `EditItemDialog`'s `updatedItem` if added to `InventoryItem` type
- Add `manufacturerNotes?: string` and `additionalNotes?: string` to `InventoryItem` for consistency
- In add flow, `newItemData` spreads `manufacturerNotes` and `additionalNotes` from form, storing them on item object in JSON
- Keep `notes?: string` for backward compatibility, but use `additionalNotes` as canonical field for forms
- Template forms map `data.additionalNotes` to `notes` for storage The runtime item may have additional keys, so the InventoryItem type should include them. Optional manufacturerNotes and additionalNotes fields should be added to InventoryItem for consistency.

For backward compatibility when loading edit forms:
- Use additionalNotes only, migrating notes data: `additionalNotes: item.additionalNotes ?? item.notes`
- This approach avoids duplication while preserving existing data in notes field When submitting, save both `manufacturerNotes` and `additionalNotes`, and either clear the legacy `notes` field or set `notes = additionalNotes` for backward compatibility.

In `EditItemDialog`'s `handleSubmit`, use:
- `manufacturerNotes: values.manufacturerNotes`
- `additionalNotes: values.additionalNotes`
- `notes: values.additionalNotes ?? values.notes` (to maintain compatibility with legacy code)

Alternatively, simplify by using only the `notes` field for storage and mapping `additionalNotes` to `notes` in forms  a minimal change approach.

For the `EditItemForm`:
- Add `manufacturerNotes` and `additionalNotes` to `formSchema` as optional fields
- Set `defaultValues` for `manufacturerNotes` from `item.manufacturerNotes` and `additionalNotes` from `item.notes` or `item.additionalNotes`</details></think>

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
When a container is `undefined`, passing `undefined` explicitly versus omitting it entirely can matter depending on how the system handles these cases. 

- Passing `undefined` may trigger specific validation or error handling logic.
- Omitting the parameter might allow default behavior or skip certain checks.
- The distinction often depends on whether the system treats `undefined` as an intentional value or as a missing input.

In some contexts, especially with optional parameters, omitting may lead to different outcomes than explicitly passing `undefined`. When `containerProp` is undefined, the expression `containerProp || mounted && document.body` defaults to `document.body`, which is appropriate.

However, if `nestedDialogContainer` is initially null, passing `undefined` results in the portal using the body element. During a race conditionwhere the dialog opens before the container reference is setthe combobox may attempt to render with a null container, causing it to mount to the body instead.

This leads to broken behavior until the dialog is reopened. One potential solution is to use `container={nestedDialogContainer ?? undefined}` and skip opening the popover when the container is null, though this approach adds complexity. Using `useLayoutEffect` in `PopoverContent` ensures context is read after DOM updates but before paint, avoiding null context on the first frame.

An alternative approach stores the container in a `useRef` on Dialog and passes it via a context ref object (`React.createContext<{ current: HTMLElement | null }>`) so updates dont require re-rendersPopover reads `.current` when rendering Portal. export const NestedDialogPortalContainerRefContext = React.createContext<React.MutableRefObject<HTMLElement | null>>(...)

In DialogContent:
- A `containerRef` is created using `useRef`.
- The `setContentNode` function updates `containerRef.current` when the content node is set.
- `NestedDialogPortalContainerRefContext.Provider` wraps the children with `containerRef`.

In Popover:
- `containerRef` is retrieved from the context.
- The `PopoverPrimitive.Portal` uses `containerRef?.current ?? undefined` as its container prop.

**Problem**: When `containerRef` is null, the portal may incorrectly render to the body instead of waiting for the proper container, leading to layout issues during initial render or race conditions. When the Dialog opens, the Content mounts, the ref callback `setContentNode(node)` fires, and state updates to provide the new context value. The combobox, as a child, re-renders with the updated context. However, if the ref callback fires after the first combobox render, the Popover may initially render with a null container.

- Dialog opens  Content mounts  ref callback sets `ref.current`  state updates  Provider re-renders with new value.
- Combobox re-renders with updated context.
- If the ref fires after the initial combobox render, Popover may render with a null container first. When the Dialog opens, DialogContent commits first, then the ref callback fires and sets the container reference. A state update is queued, but if children flush before the Provider updates, they may still read the old null value from context. This causes Popover to render with a null container initially, leading to incorrect mounting behavior. React 18's batching could cause the Provider to still hold the old value during the same commit phase.

Using `flushSync` in the ref callback would force immediate updates but is too heavy for this case. Instead, the component should ensure that the context provider has updated before any children attempt to read it. This can be achieved by ensuring the ref fires before the state update or by deferring the child render until after the context has been updated.

- Ref fires and sets container reference.
- State update is queued.
- Children flush and try to read context.
- If Provider hasn't updated yet, children get null container.
- Solution: Ensure context update happens before The ref context approach involves using a mutable ref to hold the container value, ensuring it's updated synchronously without relying on state updates. This avoids race conditions by providing a stable reference that directly reflects the current container value.

- `ContainerRefContext` holds a ref object that remains stable across renders.
- `DialogContent` manages a `containerRef` that updates synchronously when the content node is set.
- The ref is used directly in `Popover` to access the container, bypassing context state updates.
- This eliminates the need for forcing provider updates through state changes, simplifying the flow and reducing potential race conditions.</details></think>

Our DialogContent in AddItemDialog uses `overflow-hidden` in its className override, and Popover appends to this node. If the portal container is the DialogContent element, which has `overflow-hidden`, the popover may be visually clipped. This is a critical bug because absolute or fixed-positioned popovers could be clipped by the `overflow-hidden` property on the same element. Actually, `position: fixed` popovers are not consistently clipped by parent overflow across browsers. In CSS, `overflow: hidden` on an ancestor can clip `position: fixed` elements in some cases, especially when `transform` creates a new containing block. Since Dialog uses `translate` in its className, this creates a new containing block, making `position: fixed` elements inside relative to the dialog rather than the viewport  potentially clipping them with `overflow-hidden`.

This means mounting the popover inside DialogContent could **clip** the dropdown.

Options to fix this include:
- Moving the popover outside the dialog to avoid clipping
- Adjusting z-index or overflow behavior
- Using `position: absolute` instead of `fixed` if possible Portal to an element inside the dialog tree that doesnt have `overflow-hidden` and `transform`, such as the inner scroll `div` without transform.

Or use `modal={false}` on Dialog.

AddItemDialog structure:
- `<DialogContent>` has `overflow-hidden` and `translate` (creates new containing block)
- Inner scroll `div` has `overflow-y-auto` and no `transform`
- Ref `setContentNode` is attached to `DialogPrimitive` The outer element with `overflow-hidden` and `transform` causes clipping issues for popovers.  
**Fix**: Avoid placing the popover inside this element.  
- Do not attach the popover ref to the outer `DialogContent` (which has `overflow-hidden` and `transform`).  
- Instead, use an inner wrapper with `overflow-visible` and no `transform`.  

**Alternative approach**:  
- Portal the popover to `document.body`.  
- Set `modal={false}` on the Dialog (for add/edit/quick-add only).  
- This restores pointer events to the body and allows `position: fixed` popovers to work correctly. **Alternative 2**: Increase z-index and portal to the inner scroll div  requires a second ref provider in the scroll region without overflow-hidden ancestors.

**Alternative 3**: Remove `overflow-hidden` from DialogContent and apply it only to the inner section  may affect layout. Alternative 4 involves positioning the popover content with `position: fixed` and portaling it to the dialog content. However, due to the dialog's `overflow-hidden` and `transform` properties, the popover may still be clipped even if it's positioned fixed. This is because `position: fixed` elements are relative to the viewport unless they're within a transformed ancestor, and the dialog's `transform` creates a new containing block. Therefore, the popover content could be clipped by the `overflow-hidden` on the same parent element.

Testing shows that if the portal container is the dialog content with `overflow-hidden`, the `position: fixed` popover content may still be clipped by the parents overflow settings. This occurs regardless of whether the popover is placed as the last child of DialogContent or elsewhere within it. I'll check MDN: `overflow: hidden` on ancestor clips **all** descendants including fixed in modern spec when the fixed element's containing block is that ancestor (due to transform).

So **nested portal to dialog content breaks visually**.

**Revisit**: The pointer-events fix - `disableOutsidePointerEvents` blocks events to elements **outside** the dismissable layer subtree. Portaling **into** the layer fixes pointer events but **clipping** may hide the popover.

This follows shadcns pattern for `modal={false}`. Without an overlay, clicks pass through to the page, creating a poor user experience.

Use `onPointerDownOutside` with `preventDefault`  we already prevent dismissal when the outside target is in the popper, but the problem is that pointer events never reach the popper due to `disableOutsidePointerEvents`. So nested portal must be inside the dismissable layer but outside the `overflow-hidden` ancestor.

So revert DialogContent provider to **not** use Content ref - use **optional** provider at app level. Better: **Export a small helper** `DialogScrollBody` that sets portal container to its own div.

- Add component `DialogNestedPortalsRoot` or export context + `provideDialogNestedPortals(ref)`
- Wrap inner scroll area in AddItemDialog, EditItemDialog, MobileQuickAddDialog with:

Here’s what was going wrong and what we changed.

### Combobox / selects in Add + Mobile Quick Add
Radix **modal** `Dialog` turns on `disableOutsidePointerEvents` on the dialog layer. Your combobox (Popover) and Select content are portaled to **`document.body`**, so they sit *outside* that layer and never receive clicks.

**Fix:**
1. **`NestedDialogPortalContainerContext`** (`nested-dialog-portal-container.tsx`) – the dialog panel node is stored when `DialogContent` mounts.
2. **`PopoverContent`** and **`SelectContent`** pass `container={…}` into the Radix portal so overlays mount **inside** the dialog content node (still under the dismissable layer, so pointer events work).
3. **Add / Edit / Mobile Quick Add** dialogs used `overflow-hidden` on the shell; with a transformed dialog, that **clipped** portaled popovers. Replaced with `overflow-x-hidden overflow-y-visible` and `min-h-0` so the middle area can still scroll with `overflow-y-auto`.
4. Raised popover/select **z-index** to `z-[100]` so lists sit above the dialog chrome.

No dev-server restart is required; a normal refresh is enough.

### Edit item – missing “Additional Info” / decommissioning
The edit flow used a **local** `AdditionalInfoTab` that didn’t match the shared tab. It’s now the same **`AdditionalInfoTab`** as add (company asset tag, manufacturer notes, maintenance + additional notes, photo, decommissioning block, expense / allocation).

**Schema / save:**
- Replaced **`notes`** with **`additionalNotes`** + **`manufacturerNotes`** (aligned with add).
- Defaults: `additionalNotes` from `item.additionalNotes ?? item.notes`.
- **`InventoryItem`** now includes optional **`manufacturerNotes`** and **`additionalNotes`**.
- **`EditItemDialog`** persists `notes`, `additionalNotes`, and `manufacturerNotes` from the form.

---

still not selectable?

I see a critical bug in the dialog functionality. The order of props spreading matters because `{...props}` is spread after the explicit handlers (`onInteractOutside`, `onPointerDownOutside`, `onFocusOutside`). This could cause unexpected behavior since props are spread last, meaning they take precedence over earlier defined handlers. The real issue is that the Provider value is stale on first render. `nestedPortalContainer` starts as `null`, so the initial Provider value is `null`. The Popover reads `null` and portals to the body. The ref callback `setContentNode` sets the state to the HTMLElement on first render, making the Provider value equal to the node on the second render.

However, if the Popover mounts before the combobox opens, it may not portal content initially. When the combobox opens and `PopoverContent` renders, the Provider should already have been updated with the correct value.

In React 18 Strict Mode, components might mount twice, potentially causing issues where `nestedPortalContainer` remains null during initial renders.

PopoverPrimitive's behavior depends on whether the Provider value has been updated by the time `PopoverContent` attempts to read it. The `PopoverPrimitive.Portal` component forwards the `container` prop to `PortalPrimitive`, which determines where the portal content is rendered. In the implementation, `PopoverContent` uses `PopoverPrimitive.Portal` with `container={nestedDialogContainer ?? undefined}`. This means that when `nestedDialogContainer` is set, the portal will render its content into that container instead of the default body.

- The `container` prop is forwarded through `PopoverPrimitive.Portal` to `PortalPrimitive`.
- `PopoverContent` sets `container` based on `nestedDialogContainer`.
- If `nestedDialogContainer` is null, the portal falls back to rendering in the body.
- The order of prop spreading in `DialogContent` can lead to handler overrides if `props` includes explicit handlers like `onPointerDownOutside`.

The key point is that `PopoverPrimitive.Portal` does indeed forward the `container` prop to `PortalPrimitive`, allowing for custom portal targets. The `container` prop is correctly passed to `PortalPrimitive`, which determines where the portal content is rendered. However, there's a potential issue where `nestedDialogContainer` might refer to the **DismissableLayer** root  the DialogPrimitive.Content  causing portaled children to append to it instead of the intended target. The ref on DialogPrimitive.Content is actually on the DismissableLayer, not the DialogPanel itself. The ref is applied to the outermost element in the component tree, which includes FocusScope > DismissableLayer.

- The ref is placed on DismissableLayer, which wraps the DialogPanel.
- The actual DOM node for the dialog panel is nested inside this structure.
- The ref is passed down through DismissableLayer to the innermost element (the dialog panel).
- The order of prop spreading matters because `{...props}` is spread after explicit handlers, potentially overriding them.

The key concern is that if consumers pass `onPointerDownOutside` via props, it could override the internal handler defined in DialogContent. This could break expected behavior since props are spread last and take precedence over earlier defined handlers.

- The DialogContentImpl in radix-dialog uses DismissableLayer as the ref target.

Since the overlay is a sibling element behind the content, clicks on the popover may be considered "outside" the overlay, but the popover should appear above the overlay in the stacking order.

- Clicks on the popover inside dialog content might be captured by the overlay due to pointer-events.
- The popover should render above the overlay in the stacking context.

Lastly, `onFocusOutside` on PopoverContent in non-modal Radix Popover prevents default to keep focus  this could also block clicks from propagating correctly.

- Preventing default The Dialog component can be made non-modal by setting `modal={false}`, which disables outside pointer events and allows popovers to portal to the body and receive events correctly.

- This enables proper event handling for portaled content

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
**Critical bug**: Popover incorrectly reads `nestedContainerRef?` Popover does not re-render when only `ref.current` mutates, causing it to read stale values. On first open, PopoverContent renders and reads `containerRef.current`, which should be set if the dialog is mounted before. If both dialog and combobox open in same frame, the ref might be set during the same commit. Dialog commits first, setting `ref.current` to the element, then combobox opens in a new render, causing PopoverContent to read the updated ref value. When the dialog first opens, `nestedContainerRef` is a new ref from the provider, but the provider's value is the same ref object from the parent `DialogContent`. As `DialogContent` mounts, the ref is created and callbacks fire, setting `nestedPortalContainerRef.current = node`.

Later, when the combobox opens, it re-renders and reads `nestedContainerRef.current`, which should be the node  but if the combobox was already mounted before the dialog opened, its initial render may occur before `DialogContent`'s ref callback fires, leading to a stale read.

- Dialog mounts and sets `nestedPortalContainerRef.current = node`
- Combobox re-renders and reads `nestedContainerRef.current`
- If combobox rendered before `DialogContent`'s ref callback fired, it reads stale value
- This causes incorrect behavior due to timing of mount and ref updates In React 18, ref callbacks execute depth-first, meaning child refs run before parent refs. If a child component mounts and tries to read a parent ref that hasn't executed yet, it will get a stale or null value. For example, when AddItemForm mounts, DialogContent's ref hasn't fired, so `nestedPortalContainerRef.current` is null. When the combobox opens and PopoverContent tries to read the ref, it still sees null. Only on the next commit does the parent ref update to the node, but Popover doesn't re-render, leaving the UI in a broken state. To fix the issue, a forced re-render is needed when the dialog content ref attaches. This can be achieved by using state to trigger a re-render or employing `useLayoutEffect` in the Combobox to subscribe to ref updates.

A combined approach ensures ref synchronization and forces subtree re-renders:

- Keep `ref.current` synchronous
- Bump state version when node is set to force subtree re-render

```tsx
const [, force] = React.useReducer((x) => x + 1, 0)
const setContentNode = (node: HTMLElement | null) => {
  nestedPortalContainerRef.current = node
  if (node) force()
  ...
}
```

This ensures that when the dialog mounts and the ref fires, a re-render is triggered, allowing the Combobox to read the correct container reference. Or use **state** for container **and** ref - simpler:

- Use state to track the portal host
- Update both `nestedPortalContainerRef.current` and state when the node is set
- Pass state directly to Portal as the container

Popover: `container={nestedContainerRef.current ?? portalHost}` - redundant.

- Just use state for portal container passed to Portal
- The issue was **modal** blocking body
- Using `modal={false}` alone might be enough without nested container</details></think>

Restoring a stateful portal host so Popover re-renders when the dialog content mounts (ref mutations don't trigger re-renders). Keeping `modal={false}` so a brief fallback to `document.body` works.

Here’s what was going wrong and what we changed.

**Cause:** With Radix **`modal={true}`** (the default), the dialog layer uses **`disableOutsidePointerEvents`** and scroll locking so that **clicks never reach nodes that are portaled to `document.body`** (your combobox popover and select menus). Nesting the portal in the panel helped in theory, but **reading only a ref for the portal target doesn’t trigger a re-render**, so the popover could still mount to `body` on the first open and stay broken.

**Changes:**
1. **`modal={false}`** on the dialogs that use comboboxes: **Add item**, **Edit item**, **Mobile quick add**, and **Templates** (create/edit template).
2. **`nonModalBackdrop`** on those `DialogContent`s: a full-screen **`DialogClose`** button styled like the old overlay so the dimmed backdrop still closes the dialog (Radix doesn’t render its overlay when `modal={false}`).
3. **Portal host via React state** again (`NestedDialogPortalHostContext`) so when the dialog content mounts, **children re-render** and Popover/Select get a real **`container`** instead of falling back to `body` on the first open.

After a refresh, list rows in location/rack comboboxes should take clicks normally. If anything still feels off, say which dialog and control (location vs rack vs a `<Select>`).

---

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
I discovered a critical issue in cmdk v1.1.1! The issue involves the `disablePointerSelection` flag in cmdk v1.1.1. When `disablePointerSelection` is set to true, `onPointerMove` is disabled, preventing hover selection. However, `onClick` should still function correctly and trigger `onSelect`.

- `onClick` calls `b`, which runs `onSelect`
- `onPointerMove` calls `S`, which updates state with `s.setState("value",R.current,!0)` for hover selection
- `getDisablePointerSelection` defaults to false, meaning pointer selection is enabled by default

The core problem is ensuring `onClick` works even when `disablePointerSelection` is true, while `onPointerMove` remains disabled. The `b` function handles click events by first calling `S()` to update state and then invoking `onSelect` with the computed value `R.current`. The `S` function updates the state with `s.setState("value", R.current, !0)` for hover selection.

`R` represents the computed value for an item, derived from `we(r,u,[e.value,e.children,u],e.keywords)`. This function determines the `data-value` attribute using either `e.value` or the text content of children.

The `data-value` attribute is set via `we` which uses `e.value` or text content of children, and we pass `value={`${option.label}\u2000${option.value}`}` to ensure proper value handling.

- `we` computes the value for items
- `data-value` is set based on computed values
- `R.current` holds the current item's computed value `R` refers to the trimmed string from the hook, used as the argument for `onSelect`.

The issue may stem from **Radix Popover DismissableLayer**, where pointer down on an item could be interpreted as an outside click, dismissing the popover before the click event fires.

Alternatively, **Electron** webview might have different pointer behavior.

A potential fix is to add the following to **CommandItem**:
- `onPointerDown={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); e.stopPropagation() }}` The shadcn combobox fix typically involves using `onSelect={(currentValue) => {...}}`. For dialogs, **CommandItem** requires `onPointerDown={(e) => { e.preventDefault() }}` to prevent premature popover dismissal.

From https://github.com/pacocoursey/cmdk/issues/267, selection issues arise because **CommandItem** uses **onClick** for selection. If **pointerdown** triggers the **Popover** to close first, the click event may not fire.

In **Radix Popover**, `onInteractOutside` fires on pointerdown outside  but since our item is inside the popover, it shouldn't trigger. Unless - portaled content is considered "outside" due to incorrect tree structure?

Another theory: `disablePointerSelection` might be getting set to true unexpectedly - let me search for it.

Re-reading cmdk:
- Default value for `disablePointerSelection` is false, set via destructuring assignment `disablePointerSelection:Ae=!1`
- The `CommandEmpty` component returns null when `u.filtered` has results, not when it's empty. When `count === 0` is false, meaning `count > 0`, the `Empty` component is not rendered  this is correct.

However, when the user searches "te" and `filtered.count > 0`, the `Empty` component is hidden. But since `shouldFilter={false}`, the filtering logic may not update `filtered.count` as expected.

From the code:

Here’s what was going wrong and what we changed.

**What was wrong**  
1. **`CommandItem` used `value={label + '\u2000' + id}`** while the row text is only the label. cmdk’s internal selection / `onSelect` argument is tied to that `value` string. That mismatch can break keyboard and pointer handling even if your `onSelect` closure called `handleSelect(option.value)`.

**What we changed** (in `combobox.tsx`):
1. **`value={option.value}`** so the cmdk value is the real id, and **`keywords={[option.label]}`** so labels are still available for anything that needs them.
2. **`onPointerDown`** on each item: **`preventDefault` + `stopPropagation`**, then **`handleSelect(...)`**. That avoids Radix/cmdk eating the mouse sequence inside dialogs/popovers so the choice actually applies.
3. **`onCloseAutoFocus={(e) => e.preventDefault()}`** on **`PopoverContent`** so focus doesn’t bounce back to the trigger in a way that closes the list before the click completes.
4. **`handleSelect`** still accepts the old composite string so any leftover behavior keeps working.

After a refresh, searching then clicking **Server Rooms/TF** (or any row) should set **Location** correctly. If anything still fails, try **Enter** on the highlighted row—that path uses cmdk’s `onSelect` only.

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
If stopPropagation only stops the bubble phase, the capture phase on the item runs first (target phase, then capture down, then bubble up). Actually, the order is: capture phase (from root to target), then bubble phase (from target to root).

- **onMouseDownCapture** runs during the capture phase when descending toward the target.
- For capture listeners **on the target element itself**, they execute first during the capture phase, then bubble listeners follow.
- During the capture phase, events travel from window down to the target element.
- During the bubble phase, events travel back up from the target element to the window.
- When an event reaches the target element, it can have both capture and bubble listeners, but capture listeners run before bubble ones.
- In some browsers, capture listeners on the target element may run during both capture and bubble phases, specifically at the **AT_TARGET** phase. **onMouseDownCapture** fires during the capture phase when the event reaches the target element. The capture phase moves from outermost to innermost, so the dialog's capture listener runs before the popover's, which runs before the command item's.

- Capture phase order: Dialog  Popover  CommandItem
- Capture listeners on the target element execute during the capture phase
- Bubble listeners execute after capture listeners on the target element</details></think>

**Why Enter worked but the mouse didn’t:** Enter uses cmdk’s keyboard path. The mouse path goes through **`mousedown` → `click`**, and Radix’s **Dialog / Popover dismissable layers** often handle **`pointerdown`/`mousedown` in the bubble phase** and treat the interaction as “outside” or steal it before cmdk’s **`onClick`** runs—especially in **Electron**.

**What we changed:** Use **`onMouseDownCapture`** on each `CommandItem`. Capture runs **while the event is moving down the tree**, **before** those parent handlers, so we:

1. **`preventDefault()`** – avoids focus/click behavior that was fighting the list.  
2. **`stopPropagation()`** – keeps the dialog/popover layer from treating this press as something else.  
3. **`handleSelect(...)`** – applies the same value as Enter, then closes the popover.

Here’s what was going wrong and what we changed.

### “Maximum update depth exceeded” (rack location)
The combobox had:

```ts
useEffect(() => {
  setInputValue(...)
}, [value, options])
```

`options` is often a **new array every render** (same entries, new reference). That re-ran the effect every time, called `setInputValue`, kicked cmdk’s controlled input sync, and could spiral with React/cmdk.

**Change:** keep the latest options in a **`ref`**, run the effect only when **`value` changes**, and use a **functional** `setInputValue` so we don’t set state when the string is already correct.

### Mouse still not selecting
`onMouseDownCapture` + `preventDefault`/`stopPropagation` on items was fighting cmdk’s own **`onClick` → `onSelect`** path, so the mouse path stayed broken while **Enter** (keyboard) still worked.

**Change:** remove the capture mousedown handlers. On **`PopoverContent`**, use the usual Radix/shadcn pattern: **`onPointerDown` + `preventDefault()`** so the dialog doesn’t steal focus before the click completes — **but** skip that when the event is on the **cmdk search field** (`[cmdk-input-wrapper]` / `cmdk-input`) so clicking into the filter still focuses and types normally.

After a refresh, rack (and other) comboboxes should: **no crash** on pick, **mouse click** on a row should commit like **Enter**, and **clicking the search box** should still work.

This creates a UX issue where users dont see all options when opening with a selection, as the trigger displays the selected item instead of showing it in the list. To improve this, consider setting **inputValue** to an empty string (`""`) on open to show all options initially, rather than using the label as the filter. The Shadcn pattern involves resetting the search on open and using `defaultValue=""` for the input. To implement this:

- Remove the `value` prop from `CommandInput`
- Use `key={String(open)}` to remount the input on every open
- Reset `inputValue` to an empty string when the popover opens
- Set `defaultValue=""` to ensure a clean start

This ensures the input is always fresh and empty when the popover opens, improving UX by showing all options initially. Using `key={open}` causes remounting issues because the key stays the same when the popover reopens. To fix this, use a sequence counter (`openSeq`) that increments every time the popover opens. This ensures a unique key on each open, triggering a proper remount.

- Increment `menuEpoch` on every open event
- Use `key={menuEpoch}` to force remounting
- Set `defaultValue=""` to clear input on remount
- Prevent stale input values on reopen</details></think>

That syncs cmdk's internal search on every keystroke and interacts with `setState("search")` → `J()` (auto-select first item), causing a React update loop with `useSyncExternalStore`. Fixing by making the filter input uncontrolled (remove `value` from `CommandInput`), resetting filter text when the menu opens, and remounting the input with a key so cmdk's controlled sync doesn't run.

Here is what changed.

**Cause:** `CommandInput` was controlled with `value={inputValue}`. In cmdk, that wires into an internal effect that keeps search state in sync with the prop. Together with `onValueChange` → `setInputValue` and your filtered list updates, that could keep scheduling updates and hit React’s “maximum update depth” after you picked a rack and kept typing.

**Change (in `src/components/ui/combobox.tsx`):**

1. **Uncontrolled filter field** — `CommandInput` no longer gets `value={...}`. It uses `defaultValue=""` and only `onValueChange={handleInputChange}` so cmdk’s controlled-input sync loop does not run on every keystroke.

2. **Reset when the menu opens** — `handleOpenChange` clears `inputValue` and increments `inputSession` when `next === true`, so each open starts with an empty search and a remounted input (`key={inputSession}`).

3. **Removed** the `useEffect` that synced `inputValue` from `value`; the trigger still shows the selection via `displayValue`, and opening the menu always starts from a clean search.

After a refresh, flow should be: pick rack → reopen → type to filter → no crash, mouse selection unchanged.

_**Agent (default)**_

Here is what was going wrong and what we changed.

**Why clicks failed**  
`PopoverContent` was calling `preventDefault()` on `pointerdown` for everything except the search field. Rack/location rows are `[cmdk-item]`, not `cmdk-input`, so the browser never got a normal click on those rows. The handler now skips `preventDefault` for `[cmdk-item]`, `[cmdk-list]`, `[cmdk-empty]`, `[cmdk-group]`, and `[cmdk-root]` as well as the input.

**Why you still hit max update depth**  
Search was driven by React (`inputValue` → `filteredOptions` → new `CommandItem` list every keystroke). That hammers cmdk’s internal store and item registration and can still blow the update limit. The combobox now uses **cmdk’s own filtering** (`shouldFilter` left at default): all options stay mounted, search/filter happens inside cmdk, and **`CommandInput` has no `value` / `onValueChange` to React**.

**Other details**  
- `Command` is keyed with `menuEpoch` when the popover opens so search/selection resets each time.  
- Custom rack values still work: `ComboboxEmptyBody` uses `useCommandState` from `cmdk` to read the current search and show **Add "…"** when nothing matches.

I couldn’t run `npm run check` from here because the shell doesn’t support your UNC working directory; run it locally if you want a full `tsc` pass. After a refresh, try: open rack combobox → type → click a row; it should select without crashing.

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The issue might be related to Radix UI's popover modal behavior in version 1. Popover.Root may render a focus trap or invisible layer that blocks clicks, so checking the `@radix-ui/react-popover` package for the `modal` prop is necessary.

The popover portals into dialog content, where the dialog has a nonModalBackdrop at z-50 and dialog content at z-[51]. Since the popover is inside the dialog content node in the DOM, its stacking context is within the dialog. Even though the popover has z-[100], it's a child of dialog content, so the z-index comparison between popover and dialog content's children should work correctly. The dialog overlay exists at z-50, with a nonModalBackdrop adding another layer, while dialog content sits at z-[51]. Since the popover portals into the dialog content node, it becomes a child of the dialog content, placing it above the overlay in the DOM hierarchy. The portal container is the dialog content node itself, meaning the popover renders as a child of DialogContent, not the overlay. In the DOM structure, the overlay appears first, followed by the content, making the popover appear above the overlay due to its position within the dialog content. Content (z-51) is the nestedPortalHost element, and the Popover portals into this area, rendering its content as a child of Content. This means the Popover content is inside DialogContent and appears after the overlay in the DOM structure, ensuring it displays above the overlay.

- Fullscreen Close button (nonModalBackdrop) uses `fixed inset-0 z-50`, while DialogContent is at z-[51].
- The Popover is at z-[100], but its stacking context is within DialogContent (z-51), making it appear above the overlay.
- The fullscreen button is at z-50 and acts as a sibling to DialogContent, so Content creates the stacking context for all elements inside it. Children of Content with z-100 are above siblings of Content that are z-50. The fullscreen close button at z-50 is a sibling to Content, so it's below Content in the stacking order. The fixed fullscreen button at z-50 is not covered by the popover since Content's stacking context places its children above the overlay. If the popover is portaled inside DialogContent, its panel isnt fixed and doesnt cover the full screen; instead, it floats near the trigger within the dialog. The nonModalBackdrop is fixed at z-50, while DialogContent is at z-[51], meaning the popovers z-[100] would appear above the backdrop if it's rendered as a child of DialogContent. However, if the popover is visually above the fullscreen z-50 button, it may be because the button is a sibling to DialogContent, not part of its stacking context. 

- Popover is portaled inside DialogContent, so it's not fixed and doesn't cover full screen.
- The popover floats near the trigger and is a child of DialogContent (z-[51]).
- The nonModalBackdrop is fixed at z-50, and DialogContent is at z-[51].
- The popover's z-[100] places it above the backdrop within Popover content is rendered as a child of DialogContent and uses `position: fixed` relative to the viewport. Although it has `z-[100]`, the DialogContent creates a new stacking context due to its `transform: translate`, making all descendants' z-index values relative to DialogContent. The nonModalBackdrop is outside DialogContent at z-50, while DialogContent itself is at z-51. Therefore, the popover's z-[100] appears above the backdrop within this stacking context.</details></think>

Here is what was going wrong and what we changed.

**Cause**  
The combobox popover was portaled into the **dialog content** node (`NestedDialogPortalHostContext`). With `overflow-x-hidden`, transforms, and stacking on that panel, the floating list can be **clipped** or **lose hit-testing** even when it looks fine. The extra `onPointerDown` + `preventDefault` on `PopoverContent` was also a bad fit for cmdk (easy to miss a node and block the click path).

**Changes**  
1. **`popover.tsx`** — Optional `useNestedPortal` (default `true`). When `useNestedPortal={false}`, the portal target is the default root (`document.body`), not the dialog host.  
2. **`combobox.tsx`** — Sets `useNestedPortal={false}`, removes the `onPointerDown` handler, and sets **`z-[200]`** on the content so the menu stays above the dialog (`z-51`) when it’s mounted under `body`.

`dialog.tsx` already treats `[data-radix-popper-content-wrapper]` as inside the portaled layer, so opening/closing the dialog should still behave.

After a refresh, open Add/Edit item, open the rack combobox, and click a row; it should register. If anything still fails, say whether the **trigger** or only the **list rows** are dead.

Here is what was actually wrong.

**Radix Popper** reads the **inner** popover node’s **used** `z-index` and copies it onto the outer `[data-radix-popper-content-wrapper]` node (see `@radix-ui/react-popper`). On a **`position: static`** element, `z-index` is ignored, so the computed value stays **`auto`**. The wrapper then stacks like an unlayered fixed layer and can end up **under** `DialogOverlay` (`z-50`). You still *see* the list (it paints), but **clicks hit the full-screen overlay** instead of the items—so it feels “not clickable.” Hover/keyboard can still look fine.

**Changes:**

1. **`combobox.tsx`** — `relative z-[200]` on `PopoverContent` so `z-index: 200` is real and the wrapper gets a high z-index.
2. **`popover.tsx`** — `relative` added next to the default `z-[100]` for the same reason on all popovers.
3. **`dialog.tsx`** — when `nonModalBackdrop` is set, `DialogOverlay` gets **`pointer-events-none`** so the dim layer never steals clicks; the full-screen `DialogClose` button still closes the dialog, and popovers above/below stacking are safer.

Reload the app and try the Location combobox again; mouse selection should register.

- **↓ / ↑** — move highlight (wraps within the list; no wrap past ends)
- **Home / End** — first / last row
- **Enter** — choose the highlighted row (including “Add …” when it’s focused)
- **Escape** — close (unchanged)

The highlighted row uses the same accent styling as hover, scrolls into view when it moves, and **mouse hover** updates the highlight so keyboard and mouse stay aligned. Each combobox gets a unique list id via `useId()` for `aria-controls`. Typing in the filter resets the highlight to the first row; if the list length changes (e.g. options from the server), the index is clamped so it stays valid.

Here is what was updated in `MobileQuickAddDialog.tsx`:

1. **Rack rules use the same path as the main form** — `flatLocationLabelForRack` comes from the selected row in `flatLocationPickOptions`, with slashes normalized like Basic Details (`Parent/Child`). That value is passed into `getRackOptionsForFlatLocationLabel`, so `rack-locations.json` matches reliably (including sublocations such as TE).

2. **Rack control in the Current strip** — When the location has rack presets, the searchable combobox (with custom values) is shown under the four Current chips, with a small **Rack location** label and `Warehouse` icon. It’s no longer only inside the collapsed Details block.

3. **Session prefs** — `QuickPrefs` includes optional `rackLocation`; it’s saved in `persistSelections` and restored in `hydrate` after the location is applied (so a saved rack can come back when you open Quick add).

4. **“Same as last”** — `LastSnapshot` includes optional `rackLocation`; successful submits write it, and **Same as last** restores it (toast text adjusted).

5. **Details collapsed hint** — If a rack is set, the Details summary line includes `· Rack`.

Duplicate rack combobox in Details was removed so everything lives in Current when racks apply.

_**Agent (default)**_

Here’s what was going wrong and what we changed.

**Why it disappeared for some flows**  
The rack block only rendered when `quickRackOptions.length > 0`. Presets come from matching the **last part** of the location path to `rack-locations.json`. That could fail if:

- `locationId` didn’t match any row in `flatLocationPickOptions` (so the label string was empty), or  
- The **child id** in `parent/child` is something like `te` while the rule key is `te`, but we never tried matching that id.

**What we did**

1. **`rackLocationsConfig.ts`**  
   - `getRackOptionsForSubLocationKey(subKey)` — match rules on the sub id (last segment of `locationId`).  
   - `hasRackLocationRules()` — true when any rules are loaded.

2. **`MobileQuickAddDialog.tsx`**  
   - Build the rack lookup label from the combobox row **or**, if that’s missing, from `resolveLocationLabel` (same as your chip/TE labels).  
   - Resolve presets in order: flat label → resolved label → **sub id** segment.  
   - **Show “Rack location”** when there are presets **or** when rack rules exist **and** the location is a **sub-location** (`locationId` contains `/`). In the second case you still get the same search field with **allowCustomValue**, plus a short note if there are no presets.  
   - If only a **parent** location is selected (no `/`), the rack row stays hidden, since rack rules are tied to subs like TE.

After a refresh, pick **Server Rooms → TE** (or any sub-location) and you should always see the rack search when rack config is present; opening the dropdown to type/filter should behave like before.

Display uses `resolveLocationDisplay` which produces labels like `Server Rooms/TE` (with slashes and no spaces in `resolveLocationLabel`). The filter dropdown uses `location.name` for parent items and `value={`${location.name}/${subcategory}`}` for child items, where `subcategory` comes from `location.subcategories`. However, the actual data structure uses `children` with `ItemWithSubcategories` objects containing `id` and `name`, suggesting `subcategories` may be undefined. This mismatch could cause sub-items not to display, even if the user selects "Server Rooms" as parent.

For parent filter "Server Rooms":
- Items with `location` = `server-rooms-id` (parent only) should match Items with `location` = `server-rooms-id/te-id` (child) should also match when filtering by parent "Server Rooms". The current code `item.location === selectedLocation` fails because it compares a composite ID with a parent name.

Fix:
- Use `resolveLocationDisplay(item.location, locations)` to get label like `Server Rooms/TE`
- Compare filter:
  - If selected is parent name only: match if display label === parent name OR display label starts with `parentName/` (using normalized slash)
  - If selected is `Parent/Sub` from dropdown: the dropdown uses `${location.name}/${subcategory}` for child items, so compare against that full value The dropdown iterates over `location.subcategories` which may be an array of strings, but `ItemWithSubcategories` has `children` as `ItemWithSubcategories[]`, not `subcategories` strings. So the Select might iterate over `undefined` values, making only parent options functional. Values are set to `location.name`.

For matching:
- **Normalized item label**: `resolveLocationDisplay(item.location, locations)`  "Server Rooms/TE"
- If selected is parent name only: match if display label === parent name OR starts with `parentName/`
- If selected is full `Parent/Sub`: compare against that exact value - For filter parent "Server Rooms", match if label equals "Server Rooms" or starts with "Server Rooms/" (case-sensitive).
- Filter values for sub-items should follow `${location.name}/${subcategory}` format; incorrect field usage may cause wrong values.
- Fix Select component to use `children` field similar to BasicDetails:
  - Map over `location.children`
  - Set value as `${location.name}/${sub.name}`
  - Display as `{location.name} - {sub.name}`</details></think>

Here’s what was wrong and what we changed.

**Cause**  
Rows store **`location` as list IDs** (e.g. `serverRoomsId/teChildId`). The toolbar filter compared that to the **dropdown value**, which was the **human label** (`Server Rooms` or `Server Rooms/TE`). Those strings never matched, so every specific location showed **0 rows**. “All” worked because it skipped the location check.

**Changes in `InventoryPage.tsx`**

1. **`itemMatchesLocationFilter`** — Resolve each item’s `location` with **`resolveLocationDisplay`** (same as the table), normalize slashes/spaces, then:
   - exact match on the full path, or  
   - if you only pick a **parent** (e.g. `Server Rooms`), include rows whose resolved path is that parent **or** `Parent/Anything`.

2. **Location `<Select>`** — Sub-rows used **`subcategories`**, which isn’t on `ItemWithSubcategories`. They’re now built from **`children`**, with values **`${parent.name}/${child.name}`** so they line up with `resolveLocationDisplay`.

After a refresh, choosing **Server Rooms** should list every item in that room (including **Server Rooms/TE**), and choosing a specific sub-location should list only that sub-location.

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Radix Tabs.Content uses the `hidden` attribute when inactive, unless `forceMount` is specified. When tabs are inactive, their content is hidden, which can cause layout collapse. The visible tab's content determines the container height. This prevents the panel from shrinking below 22rem when switching from taller to shorter content.</details></think>
